_comment: Independently transcribed effect-size conventions (U08 E1-S1). Hand-maintained from the cited sources, NOT generated from internal/descriptor/conventions.go: TestConventionRegistryMatchesFixture holds the registry equal to this file, so a band changed in only one place fails. Every threshold was checked against the fetched source on verified_at. labels[0] names the region below Cohen's 'small', which Cohen leaves unnamed (Pulse: 'negligible'; R effectsize: 'very small'). Cohen (1988) itself could not be fetched (access-restricted scan); Cohen (1992) states the Table 1 conventions are those fixed in SPABS (Cohen 1988) and is cited as the primary transcription.

sources.locator: Cohen (1992) Psychological Bulletin 112(1), Table 1 row 1 (d), p. 157; p. 157 note: ES indexes for tests 1-5 are absolute values

Cohen (1992) Table 1 row 7 (one-way ANOVA f = .10/.25/.40), p. 157; Example 7, p. 158: f = .25 means proportion of variance .0588 (SPABS pp. 280-284). eta^2 = f^2/(1+f^2) gives .0099/.0588/.1379, conventionally rounded to .01/.06/.14
effectsize 1.0.3 interpret_omega_squared roxygen, Rules: field2013 (0.01/0.06/0.14; same rounded values). NOT cohen1992 (0.02/0.13/0.26), which are Cohen's R^2 benchmarks from f^2 = .02/.15/.35
effectsize 1.0.3 interpret_r, Rules: cohen1988 (applies to positive and negative r alike)

Cohen (1992) Table 1 row 6 (w, chi-square goodness of fit and contingency), p. 157. phi equals w on a 2x2 table (df* = 1). Example 6, p. 158: w = .30 on a 3x4 table (6 df) corresponds to Cramer's phi of .212 = .30/sqrt(2) (SPABS pp. 220-227), so the benchmarks for Cramer's V scale by 1/sqrt(df*)

effectsize 1.0.3 interpret_oddsratio, Rules: cohen1988 (OR < 1.44 / 1.44 / 2.48 / >= 4.27, via oddsratio_to_d and Cohen's d rules); 'OR of 10 is as extreme as a OR of 0.1 (1/10)'. d = ln(OR) * sqrt(3) / pi at d = .2/.5/.8 gives 1.437/2.477/4.268

excluded.reason: Cohen's benchmarks for V are df-scaled ((.1/.3/.5)/sqrt(df*), Cohen 1992 Example 6 p. 158); a fixed band set would be wrong on any table larger than 2x2. Means plus a caveat stating the rule, no bands.
Kendall's tau is not on Pearson r's scale (tau is typically smaller for the same dependence); no tau-specific published convention was verified. Means plus caveat only.
No primary-source convention for rank-biserial r was verified (effectsize rule set unverified: page fetch failed). Means plus caveat only.
